subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a backup exclude-pattern feature with an auto-loaded `.backupignore`, or should the first core version be limited to explicit CLI-provided patterns only?
rationale: This PR adds user-facing backup flags, an implicit file-based configuration surface, manifest/JSON output behavior, and restore-safety/security semantics; automation cannot choose that product/security boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Narrow and fix before merge
options.body: Accept the feature direction only after removing or explicitly opting into `.backupignore`, applying excludes per asset root, and preserving current main backup hardening.

options.title: Sponsor broader core excludes
options.body: Keep the implicit file behavior and broader surface only if a maintainer explicitly owns the compatibility and security tradeoff.

options.title: Defer to a new proposal
options.body: Pause or close this branch and ask for a smaller replacement PR after the product boundary is decided.

recommendation.title: Narrow and fix before merge
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction only after removing or explicitly opting into `.backupignore`, applying excludes per asset root, and preserving current main backup hardening.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup-security merge history and listed repository product authority make this the best available decision owner.
